memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"Moses said to the people, 'Do not be afraid. God has come to test you, so that
the fear of God will be with you to keep you from sinning.'" - Ex 20:20 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
This verse looks contradictory at first. Do not be afraid, so that the fear of
God will be with you.

Two different kinds of fear are in view.

The first is terror, the fear that drives us away and makes us hide. Moses says
no to that. God has not come to destroy them.

The second is reverence, the awe that keeps us from treating God casually. Moses
says yes to that, and gives its purpose: "to keep you from sinning."

The fear of the Lord is protective. Someone who genuinely grasps who God is has a
steadiness that resists temptation. Joseph, alone and pressured, said, "How then
could I do such a wicked thing and sin against God?" (Gen 39:9). That was the
fear of God doing its work.

We have largely lost this. We are so keen to stress God's approachability that we
sometimes leave people with a God who is comfortable and therefore easy to
ignore.

Both are needed. Do not be afraid, because He has come to you in Christ. And do
fear Him, because He is God.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Which do you lack more, confidence before God or awe of Him?
2. Has reverence ever actually kept you from doing something wrong?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Father, give me both. Take away my terror and give me a healthy, protective awe
of who You are. Amen.
